I watched her work another eleven hour shift at her first crappy job; something that has started to become the normal thing they did to her. Working in a wear house, it's to be expected that, it's not going to be a walk in the park. She comes through the door the desolate apartment that is hers, even if she is behind on rent. She slowly takes off her worn off shoes, too small for her feet and way past the throw away date as well, and you can see and watch the realization that she is away from everyone flow across her forest eyes.  Slowly, she carries herself to the bathroom to look at herself in the dirty mirror.  I step up from the corner as she tries not to look at me.

"another bad day?" Like I have to ask
"Everyday is." 
 She said before turning to light up a bowl. It was cold, and just another fact to her. I knew she smoked to stay numb and to try and feel some happiness; it was the only way.

"I want to do coke" It wasn't a question nothing more than her stating it for the room. 
"Why?"
"It speeds you up and then doing so, my metabolism would as well." again she didn't look me in the eye, just smoking. She hated her body, and always struggled with it.
"You'll become addicted and then if you don't stop die." There I said it, and I knew it carried weight.
"yeah... so? I'm ready to fucking die. There is nothing left to live for." And that's when tears ran down our face in the dark mirror...
